resources.string: Connect or choose at least one source to continue.
Your training, read from your own data
Apex turns the readings from your Fitbit Air into recovery, strain and sleep scores, and shows where every number came from.
Your data is stored encrypted on this phone. Apex only reads from Google, Fitbit and Health Connect, never writes, and has no analytics or ads.
Demo data is synthetic and kept in a separate store. Your real data is never mixed in.
Apex reads what the Fitbit app on this phone has already synced from your band. Open that app first if it has not synced recently.
These set your estimated maximum heart rate and the heart rate zones behind strain. Everything is optional, and anything you leave blank stays blank.
Only if you have tested it. Otherwise Apex estimates it from your age, and labels it as an estimate.
Heart rate reserve needs a resting heart rate, which Apex takes from your band readings.
Enter a height between %1$d and %2$d cm.
Enter a weight between %1$d and %2$d kg.
Saved on this phone as reported by you.
Choose at least one way for readings to reach Apex. You can add the others later in Data sources.
Sign in with Google to read your Fitbit Air history and new readings. Read-only access.
Google sign-in needs an OAuth client ID that is not set up in this build. See docs/SETUP.md for the steps, or use Health Connect or a Takeout archive instead.
Finish signing in in your browser, then come back to Apex.
Signed in, but some access was not granted, so some readings will be missing. You can sign in again to allow them.
Signed in. Readings sync from Google Health.
The client ID you entered in Settings needs the redirect scheme %2$s, but this build uses %1$s. Make a new build with this ID (run the Release workflow again with it, docs/SETUP.md).
No browser was found to open the Google sign-in page. Install or enable one and try again.
Sign-in was cancelled or refused. Nothing was saved.
Sign-in could not reach Google. Check your connection and try again.
Sign-in did not complete. Try again.
Something unexpected stopped sign-in. Try again.
Read what the Fitbit app has written to Health Connect on this phone. Apex asks for read permissions only.
Health Connect is not installed on this phone.
Health Connect needs an update before Apex can read from it.
No readings are allowed yet. Apex cannot read from Health Connect until you allow at least one.
Older history: not allowed, so only about the last 30 days can be read
Older history: not offered by this version of Health Connect
Background reading: not allowed, so Apex updates only while it is open
Background reading: not offered by this version of Health Connect
The Play Store could not be opened.
Import a Fitbit export from Google Takeout to bring in your older history. You can do this any time from More, then Import a Takeout archive. Choosing it here counts as a source for now.
Planned. Open More after setup to import the archive.
Apex can tell you when your data goes stale, or when your recovery or fatigue signals change. Alerts describe what the data shows and never give medical advice. You choose which ones in Settings.
Android did not allow notifications. You can allow them later in system settings.
Scores need a few days to calibrate
Apex compares you with your own normal, not with a population. Until it has enough of your readings, a score shows as calibrating or unavailable rather than a guess.
Recovery: after %1$d days of readings within the last %2$d days
Sleep need: personal base after %1$d nights
Workload ratio: after %1$d days of history
Lengths come from the same rules Apex scores with. A Takeout archive or a history permission can shorten the wait.
Missing data is shown as two dashes, never as zero.
